issues.failure_explanation: The convergence theorems assume y^n solves the proximal subproblem (eq:mini:dc:sub) exactly with a positive semidefinite weight M. Proposition prop:proximal_to_pre identifies exactly one preconditioned sweep with such an M. No result in the paper shows that k>1 sweeps (as used in the experiments, k=50) correspond to a subproblem with a symmetric positive semidefinite weight M_k, which requires an argument on the composite iteration operator (e.g. that \mathbb{M}\succeq T implies \mathbb{M}_k - T \succeq 0). The promised proof is absent.

failure_location.quote: It is important to note that we will prove that any finite and feasible preconditioned iterations can ensure the global convergence of the whole nonlinear second-order convex splitting method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a short lemma (or precise citation to the preconditioning literature already cited) showing that k sweeps of a symmetric preconditioner with \mathbb{M}\succeq T equal one sweep with \mathbb{M}_k = T(I-(I-\mathbb{M}^{-1}T)^k)^{-1} and that M_k=\mathbb{M}_k-T is symmetric positive semidefinite, so the theorems apply verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract/introduction guarantee of global convergence 'within a finite number of preconditioned iterations' is only established for a single sweep per outer step; the multi-sweep regime used numerically is not covered by the stated theory.
issues.title: Promised proof that any finite number of preconditioned iterations yields global convergence is never given
issues.why_classification: A standard, contained argument (available in cited work) closes the gap without changing any theorem or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 6 of the algorithm backtracks until E^n(y^n+\lambda_n d^n) \le E^n(y^n)-\alpha\lambda_n\|d^n\|^2 with no fallback. Lemma lem:LSbase only guarantees termination when \alpha < 2/(3\delta t) - L (since only \|d^n\|_{N_2}^2 \ge (2/(3\delta t)-L)\|d^n\|^2 is available); for larger \alpha the loop may never terminate (the directional derivative bound is only -(2/(3\delta t)-L+\lambda_{min}(M))\|d\|^2). Moreover Lemma lem:square:summable and Theorem thm:globalconverg require \lambda_n < \sqrt{4/(3\delta t L)-1/2}-1, but the algorithm allows any starting \bar\lambda_{max}>0 (and the remark even replaces it by a maximum, which can only enlarge \lambda_n). In the reported experiments \delta t \approx 2/(3L) gives \lambda_{max}\approx 0.22 and 2/(3\delta t)-L\approx 10^{-16}, while \bar\lambda_{max}=5 and \alpha=0.2 were used, i.e. outside the theory.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the inputs to \alpha < 2/(3\delta t)-L and \bar\lambda_{max} < \lambda_{max} (or add the fallback \lambda_n=0 of (eq:line:search:til) and cap \lambda_n by \lambda_{max}), replace max by min in the remark, and acknowledge that the experimental parameters lie outside the proven regime.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, Algorithm 1 is not guaranteed to be well defined (Step 6 may loop forever) and its runs are not covered by Theorems thm:globalconverg/thm:globalconverg:M unless the inputs are restricted; the numerical experiments are run in a regime where the convergence guarantees do not apply.
issues.title: Algorithm input contract (arbitrary alpha>0 and lambda_max>0) is not covered by the line-search feasibility and convergence hypotheses
issues.why_classification: Local hypotheses on the input parameters restore well-definedness and applicability of all theorems; no proof or rate changes, only the advertised parameter freedom is narrowed.

issues.failure_explanation: The KL property of Definition def:KL holds only in a neighborhood \mathcal{O} of a fixed critical point with a \psi depending on that point. The proof applies \psi'(A(u^{n+1},u^n)-\zeta)\|\nabla A\|\ge 1 to every large n with a single \psi and constant \zeta, before convergence of (u^{n+1},u^n) is known; only boundedness and \nabla A\to 0 are available, so the limit set is a compact set of critical points. The needed step (a uniformized KL inequality over the compact limit set, plus handling the case A(u^{n+1},u^n)=\zeta where \psi' is undefined) is omitted. The same gap appears in the proof of thm:globalconverg:M.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Invoke the standard uniformized KL lemma (Bolte–Sabach–Teboulle) on the compact connected set of limit points, note A is constant (=\zeta) there, and treat separately the trivial case where A(u^{n+1},u^n)=\zeta for some n.
